rounds.text: Rushil Decor Ltd is trading at an attractive valuation relative to its assets and sector benchmarks, with a price-to-book ratio of 0.89x compared to a sector benchmark of 2x [E2, E7]. Its EV/EBITDA of 8.47x also sits well below the sector benchmark of 13.93x, pointing to an under-appreciated operating structure [E11]. Fundamental momentum is underscored by a trailing twelve-month compounded profit growth of 97% and quarterly profit growth surging by 100% year-over-year [E15, E54]. Furthermore, cash generation is exceptionally strong, backed by an operating cash flow of Rs 89 Cr and a stellar cash conversion ratio of 14.83x where profits are fully backed by cash [E24, E25]. Working capital efficiency has also visibly improved, with requirements dropping from 36.4 days to 26.7 days [E50], while rules-based screens score the stock a 72 out of 100 with a BUY rating [E51]. Conceded: the company carries a low ROE of 1.0% alongside declining multi-year share price returns [E13, E17, E18, E19].

The bull case rests on headline growth numbers, but the core profitability metrics expose a deeply weak underlying business model [E9, E13]. Specifically, return on equity languishes at an abysmal 1.0% according to filed statements, dramatically underperforming the sector benchmark of 8.71% [E9, E13, E20]. This anemic capital efficiency is compounded by a poor return on capital employed of just 4.5% in the filings, failing to cover the sector median ROCE of 10.3% [E12, E63]. Long-term shareholders have suffered absolute destruction of capital, evidenced by compounded share price growth of -8% over 10 years, -7% over 5 years, -16% over 3 years, and -18% over the past year [E16, E17, E18, E19]. Furthermore, balance sheet pressures are mounting as total borrowings increased to Rs 279 Cr in September 2026 from Rs 260 Cr a year prior [E29], alongside an inconsistent operating margin trend [E22, E23] and a severe historical drawdown risk of -94.3% [E43]. Conceded: [E25] and [E26], which show positive operating cash flow of Rs 89 Cr and free cash flow of Rs 22 Cr in March 2026.

Conceded: [E9, E13, E12, E16, E17, E18, E19, E29, E22, E23, E43]. While historical returns and margins show weakness, the bear ignores explosive fundamental acceleration where compounded profit growth hits 97% and trailing sales expand by 13% [E15, E14], with recent profit growth outperforming 1-year price growth by 115% [E47]. This operational momentum is fully backed by hard cash generation, evidenced by robust operating cash flow of Rs 89 Cr and free cash flow of Rs 22 Cr translating to a stellar 14.83x cash conversion [E25, E26, E24]. Furthermore, working capital requirements have successfully compressed from 36.4 days to 26.7 days, directly freeing up internal efficiency [E50]. The market is severely under-appreciating these asset-level realities, mispricing the stock at a steep discount with a price-to-book of just 0.89x against a sector benchmark of 2x [E7], and an EV/EBITDA of 8.47x compared to the sector's 13.93x [E11]. Finally, institutional money flow registers as positive with domestic holdings rising, and technical momentum shows the price comfortably above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E34, E33, E40], disproving the idea that current buyers are catching a falling knife.

Conceded: [E15, E25, E26, E24, E50, E11, E33, E34, E40]. While the bull points to explosive profit growth and robust cash flows, this operational acceleration has utterly failed to translate into shareholder returns, as evidenced by a multi-year share price decay of -8% over 10 years, -7% over 5 years, -16% over 3 years, and -18% over 1 year [E16, E17, E18, E19], alongside a severe twelve-month price return of -24.2% [E42]. The bull's heavy reliance on low valuation multiples like a 0.89x price-to-book ratio [E7] ignores the reality of dreadful capital efficiency, demonstrated by a dismal ROE of 1.0% to 4.15% and an anemic ROCE of 4.5% to 6.92% that severely lag sector benchmarks [E9, E10, E12, E13]. Furthermore, the bull overlooks mounting financial strain, with total borrowings increasing to Rs 279 Cr from Rs 260 Cr a year earlier [E29] and promoter holdings quietly declining from 56.39% to 55.11% [E31]. The screen explicitly flags earnings growth as decelerating alongside a rock-bottom ROE of 1% [E56, E57], proving that the asset-level discounts cited by the bull are justified by persistently weak underlying returns.
